From the PR Newswire
January 11, 1999

CHICAGOLAND CHAMBER TO HOST TWO ‘WHAT’S AHEAD IN 1999’ EVENTS

The Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce will sponsor two events this coming Wednesday, January 13 -- both at Chicago’s Palmer House (17 East Monroe Street).

The Chamber’s annual Economic Forecast will be presented at 7 a.m. in the Palmer House ballroom (4th floor) and will feature Michael H. Moskow, President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, and John B. McCoy, President and CEO of Bank One, Inc. in a discussion of economic trends and projections for the year. Admission is $20; reservations can be made by calling 312-494-6711. On site registration (cash and credit cards only) opens at 7 a.m.

At noon, Barry R. McCaffrey, Director of the White House Office of National Drug Policy, will unveil the Clinton administration’s 1999 drug control strategy to business leaders and concerned citizens. The luncheon will be held in the Red Lacquer Room of the Palmer House Hotel and is the first in a series of meetings between Mr. McCaffrey and business groups across the country. Tickets for members of the Chicagoland and Illinois Chambers of Commerce are $20; the general public $30. For reservations, call 312-494-6730.

DRUG OFFICE NAMES LEAD AGENCY

The White House Office of National Drug Control Policy awarded Ogilvy & Mather in New York a five-year, $129 million contract to handle the media buys for its national youth anti-drug ad effort.

Ogilvy & Mather will replace Bates USA and affiliate firm Zenith Media, which had been handling the buys on an interim basis since January 1998. The use of New York-based Bates angered some lawmakers, as the firm also works for tobacco giant Philip Morris Cos.

ACCOUNTS

The District has selected Ogilvy Public Relations Worldwide of New York to lead a new mass-media HIV prevention campaign focusing on black women, black and Latino homosexuals and bisexual men. The new campaign, funded by the D.C. Administration for HIV/AIDS, is called D.C. FACES (D.C. Fights AIDS: Community Excellence Stories)
